en.title: Minimum Operations to the Shortest String by Deleting Matching Letters on Both Sides
en.description:
In one operation you choose a character and delete the nearest identical character to its left and the nearest identical character to its right; if one side has none, delete only on the other side. The chosen character itself stays. Find the minimum number of operations needed to reach the shortest possible string.

The standard input/output format and examples were compiled by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: One line containing a non-empty lowercase string of length 1..100000.
en.explanation: The examples give 2, 2 and 0 respectively. The original example mixes up indices 8/4; choosing original index 4 deletes 2 and 6 and gives adbacea.
hints: At least one copy of each letter must remain, so a letter with frequency f needs f−1 deletions, and one operation deletes at most 2. Choosing a middle occurrence lets you keep deleting on both sides, so the contribution is floor(f/2).
